standards.caption: Security Standards
standards.description: Security standards are a set of criteria organizations can follow to protect sensitive and confidential information. e.g. NIST SP 800-53, CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.4.0, ISO/IEC 27001

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the compliance check normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The resultant status code of the compliance check.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: The contextual description of the status, status_code values.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the compliance check.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The container name.

network_driver.caption: Network Driver
network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.caption: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.caption: Pod UUID
pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.caption: Runtime
runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.caption: Image Tag
tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.caption: CWE UID
cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.caption: CWE URL
cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild. (EPSS).

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.caption: Vulnerability Type
type.description:
The vulnerability type as selected from a large dropdown menu during CVE refinement.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.caption: CVE ID
uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.caption: CVSS Depth
depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.caption: Overall Score
overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

vector_string.caption: Vector String
vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

caption.caption: Caption
caption.description: The caption assigned to the Common Weakness Enumeration unique identifier.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: URL pointing to the CWE Specification. For more information see CWE.

uid.caption: CWE ID
uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration unique number assigned to a specific weakness. A CWE Identifier begins "CWE" followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CWE-123.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The tactic name that is associated with the defensive technique, as defined by D3FENDTM Matrix. For example: Isolate.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive tactic, as defined by D3FENDTM Matrix. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/tactic/d3f:Isolate/.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the defensive technique, as defined by D3FENDTM Matrix. For example: IO Port Restriction.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive technique, as defined by D3FENDTM Matrix. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:IOPortRestriction/.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive technique, as defined by D3FENDTM Matrix. For example: D3-IOPR.

d3f_tactic.caption: MITRE DEFEND™ Tactic
d3f_tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated with a countermeasure, as defined by D3FEND MatrixTM.

d3f_technique.caption: MITRE DEFEND™ Technique
d3f_technique.description: The Defend Technique object describes the technique ID and/or name associated with a countermeasure, as defined by D3FEND MatrixTM.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the data policy that governs data handling and security measures related to classification.

data_lifecycle_state.caption: Data Lifecycle State
data_lifecycle_state.description: The name of the stage or state that the data was in. E.g., Data-at-Rest, Data-in-Transit, etc.

data_lifecycle_state_id.caption: Data Lifecycle State ID
data_lifecycle_state_id.description: The stage or state that the data was in when it was assessed or scanned by a data security tool.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: Specific pattern, algorithm, fingerpint, or model used for detection.

detection_system.caption: Detection System
detection_system.description: The name of the type of data security tool or system that the finding, detection, or alert originated from. E.g., Endpoint, Secure Email Gateway, etc.

detection_system_id.caption: Detection System ID
detection_system_id.description: The type of data security tool or system that the finding, detection, or alert originated from.

pattern_match.caption: Pattern Match
pattern_match.description: A text, binary, file name, or datastore that matched against a detection rule.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the policy that triggered the finding.

rpc_interface.caption: Remote Procedure Call Interface
rpc_interface.description: The RPC Interface object describes the details pertaining to the remote procedure call interface.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autoscale_uid.caption: Autoscale UID
autoscale_uid.description: The unique identifier of the cloud autoscale configuration.

boot_time.caption: Boot Time
boot_time.description: The time the system was booted.

boot_time_dt.caption: Boot Time
boot_time_dt.description: The time the system was booted.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

created_time.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time

first_seen_time.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

first_seen_time_dt.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time_dt.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

groups.description: The group names to which the device belongs. For example: <code>["Windows Laptops", "Engineering"]<code/>.

hypervisor.caption: Hypervisor
hypervisor.description: The name of the hypervisor running on the device. For example, Xen, VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox, etc.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The image used as a template to run the virtual machine.

imei.caption: IMEI
imei.description: The International Mobile Station Equipment Identifier that is associated with the device.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The device IP address, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

is_compliant.caption: Compliant Device
is_compliant.description: The event occurred on a compliant device.

is_managed.caption: Managed Device
is_managed.description: The event occurred on a managed device.

is_personal.caption: Personal Device
is_personal.description: The event occurred on a personal device.

is_trusted.caption: Trusted Device
is_trusted.description: The event occurred on a trusted device.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

last_seen_time_dt.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time_dt.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

name.description:
The alternate device name, ordinarily as assigned by an administrator.

Note: The Name could be any other string that helps to identify the device, such as a phone number; for example 310-555-1234.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

network_interfaces.caption: Network Interfaces
network_interfaces.description:
The network interfaces that are associated with the device, one for each unique MAC address/IP address/hostname/name combination.

Note: The first element of the array is the network information that pertains to the event.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the device.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The region where the virtual machine is located. For example, an AWS Region.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.description: The device type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

bios_ver.caption: BIOS Version
bios_ver.description: The BIOS version. For example: LENOVO G5ETA2WW (2.62).

chassis.caption: Chassis
chassis.description: The chassis type describes the system enclosure or physical form factor. Such as the following examples for Windows Windows Chassis Types

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

cpu_cores.caption: CPU Cores
cpu_cores.description: The number of processor cores in all installed processors. For Example: 42.

cpu_count.caption: CPU Count
cpu_count.description: The number of physical processors on a system. For example: 1.

cpu_speed.caption: Processor Speed
cpu_speed.description: The speed of the processor in Mhz. For Example: 4200.

cpu_type.caption: Processor Type

data.description: The managed entity content as a JSON object.

device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The group object associated with an entity such as user, policy, or rule.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the managed entity.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit relevant to the event or object.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Describes details of a managed policy.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The managed entity type. For example: policy, user, organizational unit, device.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of the Managed Entity. It is recommended to also populate the type attribute with the associated label, or the source specific name if Other.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The identifier of the managed entity.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that pertains to the event or object.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the managed entity. For example: 1.2.3.

correlation_uid.caption: Correlation UID
correlation_uid.description: The unique identifier used to correlate events.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

event_code.caption: Event Code
event_code.description: The Event ID or Code that the product uses to describe the event.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.caption: Schema Extensions
extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description:
The list of category labels attached to the event or specific attributes. Labels are user defined tags or aliases added at normalization time.

For example: ["network", "connection.ip:destination", "device.ip:source"]

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The audit level at which an event was generated.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The event log name. For example, syslog file name or Windows logging subsystem: Security.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example, Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version that specifies the format of the original event. For example syslog version or Cisco Log Schema Version.

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description:
The time when the logging system collected and logged the event.

This attribute is distinct from the event time in that event time typically contain the time extracted from the original event. Most of the time, these two times will be different.

logged_time_dt.caption: Logged Time
logged_time_dt.description:
The time when the logging system collected and logged the event.

This attribute is distinct from the event time in that event time typically contain the time extracted from the original event. Most of the time, these two times will be different.

loggers.caption: Loggers
loggers.description: An array of Logger objects that describe the devices and logging products between the event source and its eventual destination. Note, this attribute can be used when there is a complex end-to-end path of event flow.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_time.caption: Original Time
original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source. For example, the time in the original format from system event log such as Syslog on Unix/Linux and the System event file on Windows. Omit if event is generated instead of collected via logs.

processed_time.caption: Processed Time
processed_time.description: The event processed time, such as an ETL operation.

processed_time_dt.caption: Processed Time
processed_time_dt.description: The event processed time, such as an ETL operation.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.caption: Profiles
profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.

uid.caption: Event UID
uid.description: The logging system-assigned unique identifier of an event instance.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the metric.

base_address.caption: Base Address
base_address.description: The memory address where the module was loaded.

file.caption: File
file.description: The module file object.

function_name.caption: Function Name
function_name.description: The entry-point function of the module. The system calls the entry-point function whenever a process or thread loads or unloads the module.

load_type.caption: Load Type
load_type.description: The load type, normalized to the caption of the load_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

load_type_id.caption: Load Type ID
load_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for how the module was loaded in memory.

start_address.caption: Start Address
start_address.description: The start address of the execution.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The module type.

boundary.caption: Boundary
boundary.description:
The boundary of the connection, normalized to the caption of 'boundary_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary(same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

boundary_id.caption: Boundary ID
boundary_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the boundary of the connection.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary (same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

direction.caption: Direction
direction.description: The direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email, normalized to the caption of the direction_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

direction_id.caption: Direction ID
direction_id.description: The normalized identifier of the direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email.

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The TCP/IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). See Protocol Numbers. For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The TCP/IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). Use -1 if the protocol is not defined by IANA. See Protocol Numbers. For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The authenticated user or service session.

tcp_flags.caption: TCP Flags
tcp_flags.description: The network connection TCP header flags (i.e., control bits).

uid.caption: Connection UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the connection.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

port.caption: Port
port.description: The port used for communication within the network connection.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The network proxy information pertaining to a specific endpoint. This can be used to describe information pertaining to network address translation (NAT).

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network endpoint type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname associated with the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address associated with the network interface.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The MAC address of the network interface.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the network interface.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful in merger or acquisition situations. For example, when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

subnet_prefix.caption: Subnet Prefix Length
subnet_prefix.description: The subnet prefix length determines the number of bits used to represent the network part of the IP address. The remaining bits are reserved for identifying individual hosts within that subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of network interface.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network interface type identifier.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the network interface.

vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The total number of bytes (in and out).

bytes_in.caption: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: The number of bytes sent from the destination to the source.

bytes_out.caption: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: The number of bytes sent from the source to the destination.

chunks.caption: Chunks
chunks.description: The total number of chunks (in and out).

chunks_in.caption: Chunks In
chunks_in.description: The number of chunks sent from the destination to the source.

chunks_out.caption: Chunks Out
chunks_out.description: The number of chunks sent from the source to the destination.

packets.caption: Total Packets
packets.description: The total number of packets (in and out).

packets_in.caption: Packets In
packets_in.description: The number of packets sent from the destination to the source.

packets_out.caption: Packets Out
packets_out.description: The number of packets sent from the source to the destination.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The full name of the observable attribute. The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the event data. For example: file.name.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Contains the original and normalized reputation scores.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The observable value type name.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The observable value type identifier.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The value associated with the observable attribute. The meaning of the value depends on the observable type.
If the name refers to a scalar attribute, then the value is the value of the attribute.
If the name refers to an object attribute, then the value is not populated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the organization. For example, Widget, Inc.

ou_name.caption: Org Unit Name
ou_name.description: The name of the organizational unit, within an organization.  For example, Finance, IT, R&D

ou_uid.caption: Org Unit ID
ou_uid.description: The alternate identifier for an entity's unique identifier. For example, its Active Directory OU DN or AWS OU ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the organization. For example, its Active Directory or AWS Org ID.

country.caption: Country
country.description: The operating system country code, as defined by the ISO 3166-1 standard (Alpha-2 code). For the complete list of country codes, see ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name as described by (NIST) For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

edition.caption: OS Edition
edition.description: The operating system edition. For example: Professional.

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The operating system name.

sp_name.caption: OS Service Pack
sp_name.description: The name of the latest Service Pack.

sp_ver.caption: OS Service Pack Version
sp_ver.description: The version number of the latest Service Pack.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the operating system.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type identifier of the operating system.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OS running on the device that originated the event. For example: "Windows 10", "OS X 10.7", or "iOS 9".

answers.caption: Related DNS Answers
answers.description: Any pertinent DNS answers information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® Details
attacks.description: MITRE ATT&CK Tactics, Techniques, and/or Procedures (TTPs) pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: Any pertinent autonomous system information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

comment.caption: Analyst Comments
comment.description: Analyst commentary or source commentary about an indicator or OSINT analysis.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence of an indicator being malicious and/or pertinent, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source or analyst.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence Id
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of collected information related to the OSINT or how pertinent an indicator or analysis is to a specific event or finding. A low confidence means that the information collected or analysis conducted lacked detail or is not accurate enough to qualify an indicator as fully malicious.

email.caption: Related Email
email.description: Any email information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

email_auth.caption: Related Email Authentication
email_auth.description: Any email authentication information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: Lockheed Martin Kill Chain Phases pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: Any pertinent geolocation information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the entity.

signatures.caption: Related Digital Signatures
signatures.description: Any digital signatures or hashes related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL of an indicator or OSINT analysis, e.g., a URL back to a TIP, report, or otherwise.

subdomains.caption: Related Subdomains
subdomains.description: Any pertinent subdomain information - such as those generated by a Domain Generation Algorithm - related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

tlp.caption: Traffic Light Protocol
tlp.description: The Traffic Light Protocol was created to facilitate greater sharing of potentially sensitive information and more effective collaboration. TLP provides a simple and intuitive schema for indicating with whom potentially sensitive information can be shared.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The OSINT indicator type.

type_id.caption: Indicator Type ID
type_id.description: The OSINT indicator type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

value.caption: Indicator
value.description: The actual indicator value in scope, e.g., a SHA-256 hash hexdigest or a domain name.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor name of a tool which generates intelligence or provides indicators.

vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Any vulnerabilities related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

whois.caption: WHOIS
whois.description: Any pertinent WHOIS information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name as described by (NIST) For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of software package.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

class.caption: Class
class.description: The class of the peripheral device.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the peripheral device.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the peripheral device.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the policy.

is_applied.caption: Applied
is_applied.description: A determination if the content of a policy was applied to a target or request, or not.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The policy name. For example: IAM Policy.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier of the policy instance.

auid.caption: Audit User ID
auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the process was created/started.

egid.caption: Effective Group ID
egid.description: The effective group under which this process is running.

euid.caption: Effective User ID
euid.description: The effective user under which this process is running.

file.caption: File
file.description: The process file object.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The group under which this process is running.

integrity.caption: Integrity
integrity.description: The process integrity level, normalized to the caption of the integrity_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source (Windows only).

integrity_id.caption: Integrity Level
integrity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the process integrity level (Windows only).

lineage.caption: Lineage
lineage.description: The lineage of the process, represented by a list of paths for each ancestor process. For example: ['/usr/sbin/sshd', '/usr/bin/bash', '/usr/bin/whoami'].

loaded_modules.caption: Loaded Modules
loaded_modules.description: The list of loaded module names.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

parent_process.caption: Parent Process
parent_process.description: The parent process of this process object. It is recommended to only populate this field for the first process object, to prevent deep nesting.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

sandbox.caption: Sandbox
sandbox.description: The name of the containment jail (i.e., sandbox). For example, hardened_ps, high_security_ps, oracle_ps, netsvcs_ps, or default_ps.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session under which this process is running.

terminated_time.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time.description: The time when the process was terminated.

terminated_time_dt.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time_dt.description: The time when the process was terminated.

tid.caption: Thread ID
tid.description: The Identifier of the thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user under which this process is running.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description: An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs that represent a process extended attribute.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name as described by (NIST) For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

feature.caption: Feature
feature.description: The feature that reported the event.

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.description: The name of the product.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the product.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the product.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL pointing towards the product.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the product.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the product, as defined by the event source. For example: 2013.1.3-beta.

bytes.description: The size of the data returned from the query.

data.description: The data returned from the query execution.

query_string.description: A string representing the query code being run. For example: SELECT * FROM my_table

query_time.caption: Query Time
query_time.description: The time when the query was run.

query_time_dt.caption: Query Time
query_time_dt.description: The time when the query was run.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the query.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing the tactics, techniques & sub-techniques identified by a security control or finding.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: The Cyber Kill Chain® provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables associated with the event or a finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the related event.

type.caption: Type
type.description:
The type of the related event, as defined by type_uid.

For example: Process Activity: Launch.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description:
The type of the related OCSF event, as defined by type_uid.

For example: Process Activity: Launch.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description:
The unique identifier of the related OCSF event type.

For example: 100701.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the related OCSF event. This value must be equal to metadata.uid in the corresponding related event.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the remediation strategy.

kb_article_list.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_article_list.description: A list of KB articles or patches related to an endpoint. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

kb_articles.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_articles.description: The KB article/s related to the entity. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of supporting URL/s, references that help describe the remediation strategy.

base_score.caption: Reputation Score
base_score.description: The reputation score as reported by the event source.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the reputation information.

score.caption: Reputation Score
score.description: The reputation score, normalized to the caption of the score_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api request.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The list of communication flags, normalized to the captions of the flag_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique request identifier.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.
